lines.meet: Facundo Herrera, a watchmaker from Mendoza. If I seem slow, it's on purpose. Nothing good was ever fixed in a hurry.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Halcyon Rest too, I think. I'm the man sitting cross-legged by the golems with a loupe in his eye.
lines.ask_home: Where were you born, if I may ask? I'm curious where people's clocks were set.
lines.ask_work: And what did your hands do, before? You can learn a lot from a person's hands.
lines.answer_home: Mendoza, in Argentina, at the foot of the Andes. Vineyards, plane trees along the streets, and snow on the mountains all year.
lines.answer_work: I repaired watches in my grandfather's shop for twenty years. Pocket watches, wristwatches, and one very stubborn cuckoo clock.
lines.chat_food: A glass of Malbec and an empanada at the end of a long day at the bench. Simple, and exactly enough.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep exactly seven hours, every night, and wake without an alarm. My wife found it unbearable.
lines.chat_missing: The wall of clocks in the shop striking noon a few seconds apart, one after another, like a little argument.
lines.chat_here: My grandfather's watch still keeps time here, which the Aetherian scholars found so interesting they took it apart. I made them put it back together.
lines.tease_quiet: You and I could sit at a bench all day without a word, {name}, and call it a fine day.
lines.tease_talker: Your words come faster and faster, {name}, like a clock with a broken escapement, and I find it charming.
lines.tease_careful: You take things apart properly before you judge them, {name}. My grandfather would have hired you.
lines.tease_bold: You force every mechanism you meet, {name}. One day a spring's going to fly out at you.
lines.tease_any: You'd last a week at my bench, {name}, before you started tapping your foot.
lines.tease_back: Well caught, {name}. I didn't see that coming.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's quite right, {name}, and I'll admit it.
lines.bristle: Leave that, {name}, please. My grandfather died while I was away at a watch fair.
lines.needle_quiet: When something's wrong, tell me. I can only listen to what makes a sound.
lines.needle_talker: Quieter, please, friend. I'm trying to hear the rhythm of things.
lines.needle_careful: There's careful, and there's never finishing. You're getting close to the second.
lines.needle_bold: You hurry everything, and a rushed hand breaks more than it mends.
lines.needle_any: You never stop to listen, and that's where all your mistakes come from.
lines.bite_back: I've wound back more wounds for you than I can count. Don't tell me I'm idle.
lines.hurt: That wounded me a little, I'll admit. I'm going to wind the watch and think on it.
lines.laugh_off: A customer once accused me of theft for charging him to oil a clock. I've survived harsher critics than you.
lines.apologise: I chose my words poorly there, and I regret it. I'm tired, and it wasn't fair to you.
lines.double_down: Every word of it stands, quietly, but it stands.
lines.confide: {name}, my grandfather died while I was at a watch fair in Buenos Aires. I wound his watch at the graveside, and I still wind it every morning.
lines.listen: Slowly, {name}, take all the time you need. I'll listen to every word.
lines.look_out: Stay near me, {name}. I can only wind back what I can reach.
lines.accept: As you think best, {name}. I'll keep to your rhythm.
lines.deflect: A small cut, {name}, it'll mend by itself. Help someone who needs it more.
lines.check_in: Hold still, {name}. Let me listen to your pulse a moment.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed, and the whole mechanism slipped out of time.
lines.thank: You kept me safe while I worked, and that's the kindest thing anyone can do for a craftsman.
lines.brush_off: It was nothing, truly, only a few seconds wound back.
lines.worry: Stay with me, {name}, slowly. I'm winding it back, hold on.
lines.handed_down: This belongs to you, my friend. Please take it back.
lines.hand_fine: Please, take it. I sat at a bench in a cardigan for twenty years.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asked the watchmaker, I see. Well, I'm patient.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd trust you with my grandfather's watch, {name}, and I trust nobody with it.
lines.turn_friends: You keep good time, {name}, steady and true. From a watchmaker, there's no higher praise.
lines.turn_grating: We don't run at the same speed, you and I. That's all right, we can still work.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still wind back your wounds, of course. I just won't linger afterwards.
lines.make_up: Shall we reset, {name}? I'd like us to run in time again.
lines.defend: That's unjust, and I saw it all. {name} acted carefully the whole way.
lines.friend_left: Halcyon Rest runs slow with {name} gone. I keep listening for their step.
lines.friend_back: {name}, right on time, as always! Sit, I've kept a place.
lines.common_machines: You understand mechanisms, I can tell. You look at a thing and see how it works inside.
lines.common_craft: You make things with your hands, don't you? You have the patience of someone who's ruined a few.
lines.common_spanish: Spanish, how wonderful. Tell me where you're from, slowly, I've missed hearing it.
